# Medical
[bold]Not a medic?[/bold] Start with [textlink="Infantry First Aid" link="CMUGuideMedicalInfantry"]. It covers everything in your IFAK and how to keep yourself and your squad alive until a medic arrives.
Injuries are tracked on each part of the body. A gunshot to the arm leaves a wound on that arm, a heavy blow can break a bone, and enough trauma to the chest can damage the organs inside it. Treating a patient means finding each of those problems and fixing them one by one.
## How Injuries Work - [bold]Body parts[/bold]: the head, torso, arms, hands, legs and feet each have their own health. Damage lands on the part that was hit. - [bold]Wounds[/bold]: damage leaves wounds on the part it hit. Untreated wounds lower that part's maximum health and can bleed. - [bold]Bones[/bold]: heavy hits can fracture a bone, from a hairline crack up to a shattered bone. - [bold]Organs[/bold]: the heart, lungs, liver, kidneys, stomach, brain and eyes each have their own health, and damaged organs cause their own problems. - [bold]Blood[/bold]: open wounds and internal bleeding drain blood, which starves the body of oxygen. - [bold]Pain[/bold]: injuries hurt. Pain slows you down, ruins your aim and can put you into shock.
## Aiming at a Body Part In combat you can choose which part of the body to aim for. The keys to cycle or pick a body zone are under [bold]CMU Medical[/bold] in the controls menu. Aiming only nudges where a hit lands; it doesn't guarantee it.
## Medical Training Most medical work checks your medical skill: - [bold]No training[/bold]: you can still use basic first aid like gauze and ointment, just more slowly. - [bold]Basic training (medical 1)[/bold]: listen with a stethoscope, see fractures and internal bleeding on a health analyzer, hook up and read a patient monitor. - [bold]Trained medic (medical 2)[/bold]: see organ damage on a health analyzer, use kits at full speed and strength, and use defibrillators. - [bold]Surgery[/bold] uses a separate surgery skill. See [textlink="Surgery" link="CMUGuideMedicalSurgery"].
## In This Guide - [textlink="Start Here: Infantry First Aid" link="CMUGuideMedicalInfantry"]: using your IFAK, for riflemen and anyone who isn't a medic. - [textlink="Diagnosis" link="CMUGuideMedicalDiagnosis"]: working out what's wrong with a patient. - [textlink="Wounds and Bleeding" link="CMUGuideMedicalWounds"]: dressing wounds, stopping bleeding and burns. - [textlink="Field Treatment Mixing" link="CMUGuideMedicalFieldCare"]: making dressings in the field. - [textlink="Fractures" link="CMUGuideMedicalBones"]: splints, casts and setting bones. - [textlink="Pain" link="CMUGuideMedicalPain"]: pain, shock and painkillers. - [textlink="Organs" link="CMUGuideMedicalOrgans"]: organ damage and how to fix it. - [textlink="Surgery" link="CMUGuideMedicalSurgery"]: operating on a patient. - [textlink="Resuscitation" link="CMUGuideMedicalResuscitation"]: CPR, the recovery position and bringing back the dead. - [textlink="Defibrillators" link="CMUGuideDefibrillators"]: the Lifepak, the AED and patient monitoring.
